proposals.title: RESOLUTION In Support of the Rhode Island General Assembly Legislation Authorizing the City of Cranston a One-Year Levy Cap Exemption for Fiscal Year 2027 Not to Exceed Five and One-Half Percent (5.5%) Under R.I.G.L. Sec. 44-5-2

observations.action: MOTION made by Councilman Andujar, SECONDED by Council Vice-President Haroian to approve the Amended Resolution, with the noted correction to line 34 to reflect 4.99%. Discussion: Councilman Buonanno noted the increase will not necessarily be 4.99%. That is the backstop. Everything is still on the table. Councilman Ritz had a hard time passing 4.99%. It is a last resort to fix the problem. For weeks he has listened to residents and reviewed the impact of cuts. He hoped to receive a budget with a 5% reduction in operating expenses. He would be more comfortable with a 4% max increase. Even 4.5% provides key services while still respecting the taxpayers. He believes money can be found to restore the Senior Center and provide additional support to the schools. Realistically, the Senior Center may need to operate leaner. The schools will still be doing more with less. He would like a breakdown from the Senior Center of what a 10% reduction in operations would look like, while preserving core functions. The residents deserve to see the analysis. He would like to set up a one-on-one tour of the Senior Center over the next week. During the tour he would like to meet with each division to understand their functions, and what services are truly essential. His MBA is in lean operations. He manages budgets and operational efficiencies daily in his professional life. He offered to collaborate with any department. He thinks it would help the body if the school administration provided a tie
observations.attribution: Council President Wall

cosponsor_evidence.context: Resolution in Support of Fully Funding State Aid to Libraries to the Full Twenty-Five (25%) Percent. Sponsored by Councilmen Campopiano, Buonanno and Council President Wall
cosponsor_evidence.excerpt: On motion by Councilman Buonanno, seconded by Councilwoman Vaziri, it was voted to adopt the above Resolution. Under Discussion: Council Vice-President Haroian, Councilmen Traficante, Ritz, Campopiano, Buonanno, Councilwomen Graziano and Vaziri asked to be added as co-sponsors. Councilman Buonanno stated that we have one of the best, if not the best Library Director in the State and we should all publicly acknowledge Director Garcia and the job that he does for our public libraries. Our libraries are the most used libraries in the State of Rhode Island and that is a tribute to the commitment that we have as a City and the commitment that Director Garcia has. He visits the library with his daughters approximately two times a week. He always has a book with him and reading is one of the most important thing we can do not only for our children but as we become adults to keep our mind sharp. Councilman Traficante stated that he goes back many years with several Directors of the Cranston Public Libraries and they have not only been superb for the City of Cranston for the children of our City, but most important they have been self- sustaining with very small appropriations from City government. Kudos to them. Roll call was taken on motion to adopt the above Resolution and motion passed on a vote 8-0. The following being recorded as voting “aye”: Councilwoman Graziano, Councilmen Ritz, Traficante, Councilwoman Vaziri, Councilmen Campopiano, Buonanno, Council Vice-President Haroian and Council President Wall
